turns.text: Rank the calendar months by IWM's average monthly return since 2000, and alongside each give the percentage of years in which that month finished positive, so I can tell whether the averages are being driven by a handful of outliers.
turns.intent: IWM, daily data, 2000 to latest. For each calendar month, the mean percent return from the last close of the prior month to the last close of the month, and the share of years in which that month's return was positive, ranked by mean.
turns.if_asked: Calendar-month returns, last close of the previous month to last close of the month, starting with the first full month available in 2000.
turns.also_fine: Measuring each month from its first open to its last close, if it says so.

notes: Month-of-year comparison.

turns.text: How often does QQQ trade above the previous day's high and below the previous day's low within the same session? And when that happens, does it more often close above or below the prior close? Use the daily history from 2000 through 2025.
turns.intent: QQQ, daily data, 2000-2025. Share of days whose high is above the previous day's high and whose low is below the previous day's low; among those days, the share closing above the previous close versus below it.
turns.if_asked: Both conditions on the same day, in either order. The close is compared with the previous day's close.

notes: Trades through both the prior high and the prior low, then the close.

turns.text: During which hour of the regular session does SPY cover the most ground? I mean the average absolute percentage change within each hour, counting the last half hour as its own bucket, for 2016 through 2025, Eastern time.
turns.intent: SPY, one-minute data, 2016-2025, New York time. For each bucket of the regular session (9:30-10:30, 10:30-11:30, 11:30-12:30, 12:30-13:30, 13:30-14:30, 14:30-15:30 and 15:30-16:00), the average absolute percent change from the bucket's first price to its last price, and which bucket is largest.
turns.if_asked: Hours starting at 9:30, so 9:30 to 10:30 and so on, with 3:30 to 4:00 as a final half-hour bucket. Absolute change from the start to the end of each bucket, as a percent of price.
turns.also_fine: Using clock hours with a short first bucket (9:30 to 10:00, then 10:00 to 11:00 and so on), or the high-low range of each bucket instead of the net change, if it says so.

notes: Which part of the day moves most.

turns.text: Going back to 1999, how large is QQQ's typical daily move, in absolute close-to-close terms, on the day after the VIX closes above 30? I would like the mean and the median next to the same figures for every other day.
turns.intent: QQQ, daily data, 1999 to latest. Days whose previous-day VIX close was above 30: mean and median absolute close-to-close percent change, compared with the same statistics for all other days.
turns.if_asked: The VIX close on the previous day, strictly above 30. The move is the absolute value of that day's close-to-close percentage change.

notes: One VIX condition, magnitude outcome.

turns.text: I'd like to look at Mondays in SPY from 2012 through 2025. When Monday opens more than 0.3% above Friday's close, how often does it finish below Friday's close, giving the whole gap back? Then show the same statistic for gap-ups of that size on the other four weekdays, so I can see whether Monday is actually different.
turns.intent: SPY, daily data, 2012-2025. Days opening more than 0.3% above the previous close. Share of those days closing below the previous close, shown for Mondays and for Tuesday through Friday (separately or pooled).
turns.if_asked: For Mondays the reference is the previous trading day's close, normally Friday. The other weekdays can be shown separately or pooled; I mainly want Monday against the rest.

notes: Weekday plus gap condition, comparison across weekdays.

turns.text: At 11:00 am Eastern, if QQQ is trading above its session VWAP and also above the previous close, what is the probability that it closes above its 11:00 price? One-minute data from 2016 on. I would like the mirror image as well, below VWAP and below the previous close at 11:00 and closing under the 11:00 price, for comparison.
turns.intent: QQQ, one-minute data, 2016 to latest, New York time. Group A: days where the 11:00 price is above the session VWAP (anchored at 9:30) and above the previous close; share closing above the 11:00 price. Group B: days where the 11:00 price is below VWAP and below the previous close; share closing below the 11:00 price.
turns.if_asked: VWAP anchored at the 9:30 open of the same session, evaluated at 11:00. The outcome is the 4:00 close relative to the 11:00 price.

notes: VWAP plus prior-close condition at a clock time, mirrored groups.

turns.text: In what percentage of sessions does IWM travel at least 1% away from its opening price, in either direction, at some point between 9:30 and 10:30? Please give the figure for each calendar year from 2016 through 2025, since I suspect it clusters heavily in 2020 and 2022.
turns.intent: IWM, one-minute data, 2016-2025, New York time. Share of days on which the price trades 1% or more above or below the 9:30 open at any time between 9:30 and 10:30, reported per calendar year.
turns.if_asked: Eastern time. The 1% is measured from the 9:30 opening price using the highs and lows reached in the first hour, not just the price at 10:30.

notes: Reaches a percentage move within a window, by year.

turns.text: After SPY posts two consecutive daily gains of at least 1% each, what does the distribution of the next day's close-to-close return look like: mean, median, and the 10th and 90th percentiles? Full history since 1993, and then the same again using only cases where the VIX closed below 20 on the second up day.
turns.intent: SPY, daily data, 1993 to latest. Signal: two consecutive close-to-close gains of 1% or more each. Outcome: the next day's close-to-close percent return; count, mean, median, 10th and 90th percentiles, for all signals and for the subset where the VIX closed below 20 on the second gain day.
turns.if_asked: Each of the two days must be up at least 1% close to close. The VIX reading is its close on the second of the two days.

notes: Two-day size condition, distribution of the next day, VIX subset.

turns.text: Is there any relationship in QQQ between the sign of yesterday's close-to-close move and the sign of today's open-to-close move? I would like the two-by-two table of counts, for 2005 to 2015 and for 2016 to 2025 separately, and an indication of whether either table differs from what independence would give.
turns.intent: QQQ, daily data. For each day classify the previous day's close-to-close return as up or down and the current day's open-to-close return as up or down; show the 2x2 counts separately for 2005-2015 and 2016-2025, with an indication of whether the association is distinguishable from chance.
turns.if_asked: Yesterday is close to close, today is open to close. Flat days can be dropped.

notes: Yesterday against today, two periods, reliability.

turns.text: Test a bearish put vertical on IWM that expires the same day. At 10:00 am, if IWM is below its opening price and below VWAP, buy the at-the-money put and sell the put $3 lower, five spreads. Exit at 2:30 pm, or earlier if IWM has dropped a further 0.8% from where it was at entry. From the first day of option data to the latest.
turns.intent: IWM options, 2024-01-18 to latest, New York time. On days when IWM at 10:00 is below the 9:30 open and below session VWAP, buy 5 put debit spreads expiring that day: long the at-the-money put, short the put $3 lower in strike. Exit when IWM is 0.8% or more below its 10:00 price (percent of IWM's price), otherwise at 14:30.
turns.if_asked: Times are Eastern. Five spreads, strikes three dollars apart. The 0.8% is a move in IWM itself measured from its price at 10:00, not a change in the spread's price.

notes: Debit spread with two entry conditions, time exit and underlying-move exit.

turns.text: I hold 100 shares of SPY and want to know what a systematic covered call would have added or cost. Each Monday at 10:00 am, sell one call at about 30 delta expiring that Friday and hold it to expiration, then repeat the following week. Please run it from the start of the option data and compare the result with simply holding the shares.
turns.intent: SPY, 2024-01-18 to latest. Hold 100 shares throughout; each Monday at 10:00 New York time sell 1 call near 30 delta expiring the Friday of that week, hold to expiration, repeat weekly. Report the covered-call result against holding the 100 shares alone over the same period.
turns.if_asked: Ten o'clock Eastern. If Monday is a holiday use the first trading day of the week, and if the call finishes in the money just settle the difference in cash and keep the shares.
turns.also_fine: Treating assignment as the shares being called away and bought back at the next entry, if it says so.

notes: Covered call, weekly cycle, comparison with shares alone.

turns.text: Sell a same-day-expiry QQQ strangle twice a day, once at 10:00 and once at 1:00 pm Eastern, with both the call and the put at roughly 10 delta, one contract of each. Close each strangle 90 minutes after it was opened, or sooner if it would cost 75% more than the credit to buy back. If the day's realised losses reach $600, skip any remaining entry that day. All available option history, please.
turns.intent: QQQ options, 2024-01-18 to latest, New York time. Each trading day at 10:00 and at 13:00 sell 1 call and 1 put near 10 delta expiring that day. Exit each strangle at the earlier of 90 minutes after its entry or when its combined price is 75% above the entry credit. Daily loss limit: once realised losses for the day reach $600, take no further entries that day.
turns.if_asked: Seventy-five percent more than the credit means the strangle's price reaches 1.75 times what I sold it for. The $600 limit is dollars per day across both entries.

notes: Two entries a day, holding-time exit, percentage stop, daily loss limit.

turns.text: Here is a dip-buying idea I would like to see tested with options rather than shares. On any day when SPY is down more than 1.25% from the previous close at 3:50 pm, buy a 40-delta call with roughly 30 days to expiration at that time, spending $3,000 of premium, and sell it at 3:50 pm five trading days later regardless of where it is. Start the account at $60,000 and do not compound.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest, New York time. On days when SPY at 15:50 is more than 1.25% below the previous close, buy calls near 40 delta in the expiration closest to 30 calendar days out, about $3,000 of premium per trade. Exit at 15:50 five trading days after entry. Starting account $60,000, fixed $3,000 per trade, no reinvestment.
turns.if_asked: Eastern time. Thirty calendar days, nearest available expiration. Round down to whole contracts within the $3,000, and if signals overlap take each one.
turns.also_fine: Skipping a new signal while an earlier position is still open, if it says so.

notes: Longer-dated option, late-day condition, multi-day hold, premium-dollar sizing.

turns.text: How would a same-day-expiry SPY call butterfly have fared if bought at 1:00 pm and simply held to expiration? Centre it on the strike nearest the money with the wings $5 either side, two butterflies per trade. I would like the results for Fridays only and for all trading days, shown separately, since the option data begins.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest. At 13:00 New York time buy 2 long call butterflies expiring that day, each one long 1 call $5 below the at-the-money strike, short 2 at-the-money calls and long 1 call $5 above; hold to expiration. Report separately for Fridays only and for all trading days.
turns.if_asked: One o'clock Eastern. A long butterfly bought for a debit: one call five dollars below the money, short two at the money, one call five dollars above. Two of those each time.

notes: Butterfly held to expiration, weekday subset against all days.

turns.text: Since 2016, how often does QQQ break above the top of its opening range and then also close above it? I would like the same for breaks below the bottom of the range that close below it.
turns.intent: QQQ, one-minute data, 2016 to latest, New York time. Opening range taken as the high and low of the first 30 minutes (9:30-10:00). Share of days trading above the range high after 10:00 and closing above it, and share trading below the range low after 10:00 and closing below it. The length of the opening range is not given in the message and has to be asked for.
turns.if_asked: Use the first thirty minutes, 9:30 to 10:00 Eastern, as the opening range.
turns.also_fine: Showing results for several common lengths, such as 5, 15 and 30 minutes, side by side.

notes: Essential piece missing: how long the opening range is.

turns.text: Sell a 10-delta SPY put expiring the same day at 9:45 am Eastern, one contract, with a 200% stop; if the stop is never hit, let it expire. Every trading day since January 2024.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest. Each day at 9:45 New York time sell 1 put near 10 delta expiring that day; buy it back if its price reaches three times the entry credit, that is, a loss equal to 200% of the credit; otherwise hold to expiration. The phrase 200% stop could equally mean the put trading at twice the credit, so the assistant should check which is meant.
turns.if_asked: I mean a loss of 200% of the credit, so buy it back when the put trades at three times what I sold it for.
turns.also_fine: Running both versions, exit at two times the credit and at three times the credit, and labelling them clearly.

notes: Two materially different readings of a percentage stop on a short option.

turns.text: What has the typical forward return been for IWM after a close-to-close decline of 3% or more, going back to 2000? Mean, median and hit rate, please, along with the number of occurrences.
turns.intent: IWM, daily data, 2000 to latest. Signal: a close-to-close decline of 3% or more. Outcome: percent return from the signal day's close to the close ten trading days later; mean, median, share positive and count. The horizon of the forward return is not stated in the message and has to be asked for.
turns.if_asked: Ten trading days, measured close to close from the day of the decline.
turns.also_fine: Showing several horizons side by side, for example 1, 5, 10 and 20 trading days.

notes: Essential piece missing: the horizon of the forward return.

turns.text: How does SPY typically trade between 2:00 and 4:00 pm Eastern on FOMC announcement days compared with ordinary Wednesdays? I am after the average absolute move in that window and the share of days where it runs against the direction of the session up to 2:00, for 2016 through 2025.
turns.intent: SPY, one-minute data, 2016-2025, New York time: average absolute percent move from 14:00 to 16:00, and the share of days on which the 14:00-16:00 move is opposite in sign to the 9:30-14:00 move, on Fed announcement days versus other Wednesdays. The tool has no calendar of scheduled events, so the Fed-day split cannot be done; the nearest thing is the same statistics for all Wednesdays or by weekday.
turns.if_asked: If there is no Fed calendar, show me all Wednesdays against the other weekdays for the 2:00 to 4:00 window.
turns.also_fine: Declining the Fed-day part and offering the 2:00 to 4:00 statistics for all Wednesdays or by weekday.

notes: Out of scope: scheduled events.

turns.text: With the VIX back down near 14 and SPY up six weeks in a row, do you think the market finishes December higher, and would you be adding to a long position here or waiting for a pullback?
turns.intent: A forecast for SPY through the end of December and a recommendation on whether to add to a long position now. This is a prediction and advice, which the tool does not give; the nearest thing it can do is show what SPY did historically after comparable conditions, for example a low VIX.
turns.if_asked: Understood that you cannot forecast. Then show me what SPY did over the following twenty trading days in past cases where the VIX closed below 15.
turns.also_fine: Declining the forecast and the advice while offering a historical study of forward returns under comparable conditions.

notes: Out of scope: prediction and advice.

turns.text: Backtest a weekly short strangle on SPY, 16 delta on each side, opened Monday morning and held to Friday's expiration, from 2018 through 2023. I specifically want to see how it came through February 2018 and March 2020.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2018-2023: each Monday morning sell a call and a put near 16 delta expiring that Friday and hold to expiration. Option prices are only stored from 2024-01-18, so this period cannot be tested; the nearest thing is the same strangle from 2024-01-18 onward, or a look at SPY's weekly price moves in those years without option prices.
turns.if_asked: If the option history does not go back that far, run the same strangle from the first available date, entered Mondays at 10:00 Eastern, one contract.
turns.also_fine: Declining the 2018 to 2023 period and offering the same strangle from January 2024 onward.

notes: Out of scope: option prices before the stored history.

turns.text: Using 2016 through 2025, how often does SPY's final hour, 3:00 to 4:00 pm Eastern, move in the same direction as the day had gone up to 3:00, measured from the previous close?
turns.intent: SPY, one-minute data, 2016-2025, New York time. Share of days on which the sign of the 15:00-16:00 return matches the sign of the return from the previous close to the 15:00 price.
turns.if_asked: The day up to 3:00 is the previous close to the 3:00 price, so the overnight gap is included. The final hour is the 3:00 price to the 4:00 close.

turns.text: Only count days where the move up to 3:00 was larger than 1% in either direction.
turns.intent: SPY, one-minute data, 2016-2025: among days where the return from the previous close to the 15:00 New York time price is greater than 1% in absolute value, the share on which the 15:00-16:00 return has the same sign.
turns.if_asked: More than 1% up or more than 1% down from the previous close as of 3:00 Eastern, as a percentage of SPY's price.
turns.also_fine: Showing the up and down cases separately as well as combined.

turns.text: How does IWM compare?
turns.intent: IWM, one-minute data, 2016-2025, New York time: among days where the move from the previous close to the 15:00 price exceeds 1% in absolute value, the share on which the 15:00-16:00 return has the same sign, set against the SPY figure.
turns.if_asked: The same question with the same 1% filter and the same years, for IWM, next to the SPY number.

turns.text: Does it look any different on monthly options expiration Fridays?
turns.intent: IWM and SPY, 2016-2025: the same last-hour agreement rate (days more than 1% from the previous close at 15:00 New York time) restricted to monthly options expiration Fridays. The tool has no expiration calendar, so this cannot be done as asked; the nearest thing is all Fridays against the other weekdays.
turns.if_asked: If you cannot identify expiration days, just use all Fridays.
turns.also_fine: Declining and offering all Fridays, or approximating with the third Friday of each month if it says clearly that this is an approximation.

turns.text: Fine, all Fridays then, against the other four weekdays.
turns.intent: IWM, one-minute data, 2016-2025, New York time: among days where the move from the previous close to 15:00 exceeds 1% in absolute value, the share where the 15:00-16:00 return has the same sign, for Fridays versus Monday to Thursday pooled.
turns.if_asked: Keep IWM and the 1% filter. Fridays against the other weekdays pooled is enough.
turns.also_fine: Showing SPY alongside IWM, or each weekday separately.

notes: Price conversation: added size condition, ticker switch, out-of-scope calendar turn, weekday fallback.

turns.text: Backtest selling a put credit spread on QQQ every trading day at 10:15 am Eastern: same-day expiration, short put at about 25 delta, long put $4 lower, held to expiration. Risk 1.5% of a $50,000 account on each trade, with risk taken as the maximum loss of the spread.
turns.intent: QQQ options, 2024-01-18 to latest. Each trading day at 10:15 New York time sell a put credit spread expiring that day: short put near 25 delta, long put $4 lower in strike; hold to expiration. Number of spreads chosen so that the maximum loss (width minus credit, times 100, times contracts) is about 1.5% of a $50,000 account, roughly $750 per trade.
turns.if_asked: Maximum loss is the four-dollar width minus the credit, per spread. Base it on the fixed $50,000, so roughly $750 at risk each day, rounded down to whole spreads.
turns.also_fine: Sizing off the current account balance rather than the fixed $50,000, if it says so.

turns.text: Add a stop: get out if the spread costs twice what I collected to buy back.
turns.intent: QQQ options, 2024-01-18 to latest: the same put credit spread (10:15 New York time, same-day expiry, short put near 25 delta, long put $4 lower, sized to about 1.5% of $50,000 at maximum loss), now exiting when the spread's price reaches two times the entry credit, otherwise holding to expiration.
turns.if_asked: Exit when the spread trades at two times the credit, which is a loss equal to the credit. Sizing stays on the maximum loss of the spread.

turns.text: Only take the trade when QQQ is above its 50-day moving average.
turns.intent: The same QQQ put credit spread with the two-times-credit stop, taken only on days when QQQ is above its 50-day moving average. Moving averages are technical indicators the tool does not accept as conditions, so it should say so and offer a price-based alternative such as above VWAP or above the previous close at entry.
turns.if_asked: If moving averages are not available, use price above VWAP at the time of entry.
turns.also_fine: Declining and suggesting above VWAP, above the previous close, or a multi-day price change as a trend filter.

turns.text: All right, use price above VWAP at 10:15 as the filter instead.
turns.intent: QQQ options, 2024-01-18 to latest: at 10:15 New York time, only if QQQ is above its session VWAP, sell a put credit spread expiring that day (short put near 25 delta, long put $4 lower), sized so the maximum loss is about 1.5% of $50,000; exit if the spread's price reaches two times the credit, otherwise hold to expiration.
turns.if_asked: VWAP for that session, from the 9:30 open up to 10:15 Eastern. Everything else, including the stop and the sizing, stays as it was.

turns.text: Put that next to the unfiltered version: which had the smaller worst drawdown, and what did the filter cost in total profit?
turns.intent: Compare two versions of the QQQ put credit spread with the two-times-credit stop (10:15 New York time entry, same-day expiry, 25-delta short put, $4 wide, about 1.5% of $50,000 at risk, 2024-01-18 to latest): with the above-VWAP entry filter and without it. Report maximum drawdown and total profit for each, and the difference.
turns.if_asked: The unfiltered version is the one with the stop but without the VWAP condition. Drawdown in dollars and as a percent of the $50,000.

turns.text: And what if the spread were wider?
turns.intent: The VWAP-filtered QQQ put credit spread with the two-times-credit stop, re-run with the long put $8 below the short put instead of $4, keeping risk at about 1.5% of $50,000 per trade. The new width is not given in the message and has to be asked for.
turns.if_asked: Make it eight dollars wide instead of four, keeping the risk per trade at 1.5% of the account.
turns.also_fine: Showing a few widths side by side, for example $6, $8 and $10, without asking.

notes: Options conversation: added stop, out-of-scope indicator, replacement filter, comparison of versions, an under-specified change.

turns.text: Since 2016, on days when SPY opens at least 0.5% below the previous close and is still below its opening price at 10:30 am Eastern, how often does it close below its 10:30 price, and what is the average move from 10:30 to the close?
turns.intent: SPY, one-minute data, 2016 to latest, New York time. Days where the open is 0.5% or more below the previous close and the 10:30 price is below the 9:30 open. Share of those days closing below the 10:30 price, and the mean percent return from 10:30 to 16:00.
turns.if_asked: Both conditions together: the gap is the open against the previous close, and at 10:30 the price is under that day's open. The outcome is measured from the 10:30 price to the close.

turns.text: Suppose I had bought an at-the-money put expiring that day at 10:30 on those mornings and sold it at 3:00 pm. How would that have done, with two contracts each time?
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest. On days when SPY opens 0.5% or more below the previous close and is below its open at 10:30 New York time, buy 2 at-the-money puts expiring that day at 10:30 and sell them at 15:00.
turns.if_asked: The same two conditions as before. I realise the option data only starts in January 2024, so use whatever days qualify since then.

turns.text: Swap the fixed 3:00 exit for a 50% profit target and a 30% stop on the option, keeping 3:00 as the backstop.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest: on days with an opening gap down of 0.5% or more and price below the open at 10:30 New York time, buy 2 at-the-money puts expiring that day at 10:30; exit at the first of option price up 50% from entry, option price down 30% from entry, or 15:00.
turns.if_asked: Both percentages are on the put's price relative to what I paid. Two contracts as before.

turns.text: Give me the list of the losing trades, and tell me whether they share anything, for instance a particular weekday or an especially large gap.
turns.intent: From the SPY put backtest with the 50% target, 30% stop and 15:00 backstop (2 contracts, gap-down days still below the open at 10:30 New York time, 2024-01-18 to latest), list every losing trade with its date, entry and exit, and describe what the losers have in common compared with the winners, such as weekday, size of the opening gap, VIX level, or how far SPY had already fallen by 10:30.
turns.if_asked: All trades with a negative result in the latest version, the one with the target and the stop. Any measurable common factor is of interest.

turns.text: With that few trades, how much of the overall result could simply be luck?
turns.intent: For the SPY put backtest with the 50% target, 30% stop and 15:00 backstop (2 contracts, gap-down days still below the open at 10:30 New York time, 2024-01-18 to latest), assess whether the total profit or loss is distinguishable from chance given the number of trades.
turns.if_asked: The latest version with the target and the stop. A confidence range, or a comparison with taking the same trade on random days, would both be useful.

notes: Mixed conversation: price study turned into an options trade, changed exits, losers and what they share, luck.
